subject: EdgeScale MSA review — output ownership, training & feedback license
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@edgescale.com>

Cc: EdgeScale Legal <legal@edgescale.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — training / output ownership questions

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo last week — the product looked solid and the team is excited about the dedicated capacity option. Our legal team attached a marked-up MSA (see EdgeScale_MSA_Redlines_20260913.pdf) with a few specific asks that we need clarified before we can advance procurement:

1) Output ownership: we propose explicit assignment of customer-generated output for application features that are produced from Customer prompts (Section 3.2 in your MSA). We want a clear carve-out so EdgeScale can commercialize outputs it creates via the integration.

2) Training / feedback license: the redline adds a limited, revocable license for Redwood to use telemetry/feedback for model improvement but only on opt-in customers and with strict de-id rules. Can you confirm Redwood's policy and whether a carve-out for enterprise customers is possible?

3) Telemetry & data retention: requested a 90-day retention window for raw logs and an evidence path for SOC2 telemetry controls.

We'd like to align on these items this week. Can you and your legal lead take a look and propose counterlanguage? If it's easier, happy to hop on a 30-minute call — legal + procurement available Tue/Wed morning PT.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Commercial Contracts
EdgeScale

Attachments: EdgeScale_MSA_Redlines_20260913.pdf (pdf)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — training / output ownership questions

Hi Maya — thanks for the markup and for surfacing the three items. We're very keen to keep this moving. Quick answers up front and then next steps:

- Output ownership: we can offer a customer output carve-out for "Customer Generated Output" produced solely from Customer prompts where the Customer provides the prompt and receives the output. We need to align on a short definition and ensure it doesn't extend to aggregated model weights or derivative model products.

- Training/feedback license: Redwood's standard stance is that opt-out by default but customers can opt in to allow telemetry/feedback usage for model improvements. For enterprise customers like EdgeScale we can offer an explicit opt-in clause and tighter de-identification commitments.

- Telemetry & retention: we can provide SOC2 evidence and support a 90-day window for raw request logs if combined with an auditable deletion workflow and an exception process for troubleshooting.

I'll loop in Ben (sales) and Irene (legal) — Ben can coordinate the commercial play (order form & pricing), Irene can propose redline-friendly language.

I'm available for a call Wed 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 8:30-9:30 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: suggested language + commercial thoughts for EdgeScale requests

Ava / Irene / Grace —

I reviewed EdgeScale's redlines. High-level recomendation and suggested counterlanguage below. Keeping this internal for now.

Commercial note: EdgeScale is near a 500k ARR tier if they go Dedicated; offering the output carve-out with a small uplift to commitment looks reasonable.

Suggested positions (we should be prepared to concede some):
- Output ownership: offer a defined "Customer Generated Output" carve-out limited to non-derivative outputs (UI responses, reports, transcripts). Reject assignment of any model artifacts or datasets.
- Training license: offer an "Opt-In Training License" for enterprise that is revocable and scope-limited (only telemetry/prompt/response pairs explicitly consented to; retention limited).
- Telemetry: accept 90-day retention for raw logs with SRM (security review) + contractually defined deletion procedure; require an exception window for incident response of up to 6 months if legally necessary.

Draft redline snippet (for Irene to convert to bulletproof legal language):
"Customer Generated Output. For clarity, Customer retains title to output generated solely in response to Customer-provided prompts ("Customer Generated Output"). Redwood retains no ownership in Customer Generated Output, provided however that Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive license to use anonymized and aggregated Customer Generated Output solely to maintain and operate the Service. This Section does not permit Redwood to use Customer Generated Output to train or improve model weights absent Customer's express, written opt-in."

For the training license: propose an exhibit where EdgeScale checks an "opt-in" box on the order form and specifies if telemetry can be used for research/production model updates.

I'll be available on the call to cover commercial terms.

—Ben
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@edgescale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — output ownership, training license proposal

Maya — thanks again for the redlines and flex on timing. Attached are two items: Redwood_Response_Redlines_20260915.docx (we converted the PDF to suggested counterlanguage) and a proposed Order Form exhibit that introduces an explicit opt-in checkbox for "Training/Feedback License". Key points summarized below so legal can skim:

- Customer Generated Output: we propose the carve-out language below. It covers UI responses, exported data, and reports. Does not include model weights or derivative model products.
- Training/Feedback License: enterprise opt-in on order form. If EdgeScale opts in, Redwood will only use de-identified telemetry as described in Exhibit B and will provide a monthly report of what telemetry was used. Opt-in can be revoked with 30 days' notice; previously used telemetry will not be incorporated into new production model weights after revocation.
- Telemetry retention: agree to 90-day raw log retention with explicit deletion SLA in Exhibit C. Incident exceptions limited to documented investigations; Redwood will notify EdgeScale and provide evidence for any retention past 90 days.

If this matches EdgeScale's expectations, I can circulate a DocuSign envelope with the redlined MSA + order form for signatures and route to procurement. If there are specific wordsmithing items, Irene is happy to take a pass. Proposed next step: 30-min call Thu 09:00 PT to walk legal through the doc.
